content.user_title: Audit Paid Conversion Tracking Before Launch
content.value_statement: Paid campaigns can launch with broken events, inconsistent UTMs, and duplicate conversions. This skill checks supplied evidence and produces a launch decision, remediation list, UTM convention, and conversion event specification.
actual_capabilities: Checks a manual conversion against GA4 event name, value, currency, and acquisition source.
Marks each preflight item as pass, fail, or needs-input from supplied evidence.
Reviews UTM coverage, casing, vocabulary, auto-tagging conflicts, and prohibited personal data.
Confirms that deduplication ownership and attribution windows are declared across advertising platforms.
Builds account-specific UTM naming rules and conversion event specifications.
limitations: Requires user-provided GA4 Conversions and Traffic-acquisition exports for evidence-based results.
Does not access advertising, analytics, pixel, or tag-manager APIs by itself.
Does not reconcile individual order IDs, quantify overlap, or calculate incrementality.
Cannot mark manual event firing as passed without a completed test conversion.

use_cases.title: Validate a campaign launch
use_cases.description: Check event firing, UTM consistency, deduplication ownership, and attribution windows before increasing paid media spend.

use_cases.title: Standardize measurement specifications
use_cases.description: Create shared UTM rules and conversion event definitions for analytics and implementation teams.

use_cases.title: Review client tracking evidence
use_cases.description: Turn client exports and a manual test into a clear launch decision and prioritized remediation list.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic tracking preflight
prompt_templates.prompt: Review conversion tracking for [site] on [platforms]. Use the attached GA4 Conversions and Traffic-acquisition exports. Mark every check pass, fail, or needs-input.
prompt_templates.scenario: A marketer needs a simple launch-readiness assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Build UTM and event standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a UTM convention for [campaign goal], [audience], and [platforms]. Define purchase, lead, and signup events with values, currencies, and deduplication identifiers.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs consistent campaign naming and event contracts.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose acquisition inconsistencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the attached landing URLs with GA4 source and medium rows. Identify missing tags, casing differences, vocabulary drift, and auto-tagging conflicts. Recommend exact corrections.
prompt_templates.scenario: GA4 acquisition rows do not match campaign naming.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a multi-platform launch gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Review Google and Meta using the attached exports and manual test result. Gate deduplication, attribution windows, offline imports, and iOS modeled gaps. Provide prioritized fixes and handoff notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced launch needs cross-platform signal governance.

output_examples.input: Google and Meta launch with one GA4 purchase test and both exports attached.
output: Launch status: fix first. The purchase event fired with value and currency.
Fail: Meta landing links use mixed source values. Standardize the source before launch.
Needs input: Google attribution window was not provided.

output_examples.input: Create UTM standards for a paid search and paid social acquisition campaign.
output: Convention: use lowercase platform sources and one approved medium per channel.
Campaign names follow goal, audience, and month.
Personal data and order identifiers are prohibited in campaign parameters.

best_practices: Provide fresh GA4 exports covering the same period and timezone.
Run one real test conversion before requesting the audit.
State each platform's attribution window and intended source of truth.
anti_patterns: Do not treat missing evidence as a passing result.
Do not place emails, names, or order identifiers in UTM values.
Do not use this skill for detailed order-level reconciliation or incrementality analysis.

faq.question: What inputs are required?
faq.answer: Provide the site, platforms, important conversion actions, GA4 Conversions export, Traffic-acquisition export, and one manual test result.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to advertising platforms?
faq.answer: No. It works from user-provided exports and test evidence unless the host separately provides approved connectors.

faq.question: What happens without a manual test conversion?
faq.answer: The event-firing check remains needs-input and cannot receive a passing result.

faq.question: Can it resolve Meta and Google double counting?
faq.answer: It verifies that a deduplication rule exists, but detailed order matching and overlap measurement require a reconciliation workflow.

faq.question: What does the final report include?
faq.answer: It includes launch status, checklist results, exact fixes, UTM rules, event specifications, modeled-gap flags, and handoff notes.

faq.question: Does the skill save results automatically?
faq.answer: No. It asks for permission before writing reports or unresolved items to the documented memory paths.
